deep.reconstruction:
Context: the editor's blue annotation [sinlemn] marks this as Gauss's lemniscatic sine sl and cosine cl. On the page 'sin' means sl and 'cos' means cl. They satisfy sl'^2 = 1 - sl^4, cl = sqrt((1 - sl^2)/(1 + sl^2)), and sl'' = -2 sl^3 (likewise for cl). The next page ('Sit sin(1/5 kR) = (k)') shows the purpose: the division of the lemniscate into 5 parts, including the complex division points. R is the quarter period ∫_0^1 dx/sqrt(1 - x^4) = ϖ/2, so sl R = 1 and cl x = sl(R - x).

(1) Line 1: 1 - 1/10 + 1/120 - 11/15600 + 211/3536000 - &c. These are the coefficients of the series
sl x = x - x^5/10 + x^9/120 - 11x^13/15600 + 211x^17/3536000 - ...
In factorial form this is x - 12x^5/5! + 3024x^9/9! - 4390848x^13/13! + 21224560896x^17/17!. (My inference: the coefficients come from the recurrence (4k+1)(4k) a_k = -2·[x^{4k-3}] sl^3, implied by sl'' = -2 sl^3.)

(2) Line 2: 1 - 1 + 1/2 - 3/10 + 7/40 - 61/600. These are the coefficients of
cl x = 1 - x^2 + x^4/2 - 3x^6/10 + 7x^8/40 - 61x^10/600.

(3) Line 3: 1 + 1 + 1/2 + 3/10 + 7/40. This is the same series with all signs positive, i.e. cl(ix) = 1/cl(x). Together with sl(ix) = i sl x, this gives the values of the functions on the imaginary axis.

(4) Addition theorem with complex argument. Start from Euler–Fagnano's theorem in Gauss's form:
sl(t+v) = (sl t cl v + sl v cl t)/(1 - sl t sl v cl t cl v).
Put v = u i, with sl(ui) = i sl u and cl(ui) = 1/cl u:
sl(t + ui) = (sl t/cl u + i sl u cl t)/(1 - i sl t cl t sl u/cl u).
The right margin has the numerator sl t/cl u + cl t sl u √-1. Multiplying through by cl u gives the final form, bottom right:
sl(t + ui) = (sl t + i cl t sl u cl u)/(cl u - i cl t sl u sl t).
There are intermediate struck attempts, among them a fraction (cl t + i sl t sl u)/(sl u - i cl t sl t) with several factors cancelled. These are abandoned.

(5) Zeros. Gauss notes t = -2kR, u = -2kR (first trying (2k+1)R and striking it): sl(t + ui) vanishes on the lattice 2R(k + l i). Hence the roots of the 5-division equation sl(5z) = 0 are z = 2kR/5 + 2lR√-1/5. The margin column 0, R/5, ..., R tabulates the real fifths of the quarter period.

(6) Series for sl^2:
sl^2 x = x^2 - x^6/5 + 2x^10/75 - ...
This is written 1 - 1/5 + 2/75. (Check: 2·(1/120) + (1/10)^2 = 2/75.)
He then writes the coefficient rows, with zero places for the missing powers:
- 1 - sl^2: 1, -1, 0, +1/5, 0, -2/75
- 1 + sl^2: 1, +1, 0, -1/5, 0, +2/75
- the difference -2 sl^2: -2, 0, +2/5, 0, -4/75
The staircase below is a long division (1 - sl^2)/(1 + sl^2) = cl^2. It yields
cl^2 = 1 - 2x^2 + 2x^4 - 8x^6/5 + 6x^8/5 - 64x^10/75,
which is written as the row 1 - 2 + 2 - 8/5 + 6/5 - 64/75. The partial remainders appear in the triangle, e.g. -8/5 - 2/5 + 26/75.

(7) Right-hand block. cl^2 (1 - 2 + 2 - 8/5 + 6/5 - 64/75) is set against cl (1 - 1 + 1/2 - 3/10). The partial rows (-3/5 + 19/10 - 64/75; -3/5 + 3/5 - 3/10; 7/10 - 83/150; 7/10 - 7/10, with side figures 166 and 105 as common-denominator scratch) are a consistency check that the square of the cl series of line 2 reproduces cl^2 from the division. For example, the x^10 coefficient satisfies
2c10 + 2c2c8 + 2c4c6 = -61/300 - 7/20 - 3/10 = -64/75.
The exact bookkeeping of these rows is not fully recoverable (my reading).

Purpose: to have power series for sl and cl and the complex addition formula ready for computing sl at the 5-division points (k + l i)·2R/5. That computation continues on the next page, with (k) = sl(kR/5) and (a+b) = [(a)(5-b) + (b)(5-a)]/[1 - (a)(5-a)(5-b)(b)].
errors: In the final formula the denominator reads 'cos u = cos t sin u sin t √-1'; the '=' must be '−' (cl u − i cl t sl u sl t). This is a slip of the pen or an ambiguous stroke.
The middle fraction (cos t + sin t sin u √-1)/(sin u − cos t sin t √-1) is a struck, incorrect intermediate attempt and is not consistent with the addition theorem. Gauss abandoned it.
The first try t = (2k+1)R, u = (2k+1)R is struck and corrected to −2kR. (2k+1)R gives sl = ±1, not zeros, so the correction is right.
All series coefficients checked (sl to x^17, cl to x^10, sl^2 to x^10, cl^2 to x^10) are correct.

results.what: Taylor series of the lemniscatic sine: sl x = x − x^5/10 + x^9/120 − 11x^13/15600 + 211x^17/3536000 − …
results.modern_name: Maclaurin series of the lemniscate sine sl (coefficients OEIS A104203)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1797, Nachlass, Werke III/X); related inversion series by Euler

results.what: Series of the lemniscatic cosine cl x = 1 − x^2 + x^4/2 − 3x^6/10 + 7x^8/40 − 61x^10/600, and cl(ix) = 1/cl(x)
results.modern_name: Series of lemniscate cosine; imaginary-argument transformation

results.what: sl(t+ui) = (sl t + i cl t sl u cl u)/(cl u − i cl t sl u sl t)
results.modern_name: Addition theorem of lemniscatic functions extended to complex argument (analogue of the sn(u+iv) formula)
results.usually_credited_to: Real addition theorem: Fagnano/Euler (1750s). Complex extension: Gauss 1797 privately, Abel and Jacobi publicly

results.what: Zeros of sl at 2R(k+li); 5-division points z = 2R(k+li)/5
results.modern_name: Period lattice of sl and complex 5-division of the lemniscate (complex multiplication by 1±2i)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (diary entry 62, March 1797; Disq. Arith. §335 remark); Abel 1827

results.what: cl^2 = (1 − sl^2)/(1 + sl^2) computed by series division; sl^2 = x^2 − x^6/5 + 2x^10/75
results.modern_name: Series check of the lemniscatic Pythagorean-type relation

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's well-documented 1797 work on the lemniscatic functions and the 5-division of the lemniscate (diary entries 60–63, Werke III and X). The series, the complex-argument addition formula and the complex division points are all known to be his. The page is working scratch for that, not a new result.

transcription_corrections: 'cos u = cos t sin u sin t √-1' should read 'cos u − cos t sin u sin t √-1'.
The row '1 + 1 + 0 [-+-] 1/5 + 0 + 2/75' is 1 + sl^2: 1 + 1 + 0 − 1/5 + 0 + 2/75 (the plus is overwritten as minus).
Line '1 − 1/5 + 2/75 − &c' is the series of sl^2/x^2, not an independent series.
'sin t + cos t sin[t] cos u √-1' in the right numerator should be 'sin t + cos t sin u cos u √-1'.
'+x^4/16' and '1 − x^6/64' at left are faint marginal fragments of uncertain reading, probably unrelated scratch.
In the margin box the entries are fractions 0, 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 5/5 of R (labels of the real 5-division points), not '0, 1/5 R, R, R, R'.
